### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**1** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **144** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5f4a3f088cd7018aef904a9f31ab6b071251733c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b1b7e98e31d1236b1d2820138bd487f5204f891f` — the merge of head `d972d18be0dd135ba8362c53bbeb9d4612cf5f81` into base `5f4a3f088cd7018aef904a9f31ab6b071251733c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b1b7e98e31d1236b1d2820138bd487f5204f891f && git checkout b1b7e98e31d1236b1d2820138bd487f5204f891f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 5f4a3f088cd7018aef904a9f31ab6b071251733c d972d18be0dd135ba8362c53bbeb9d4612cf5f81 && git checkout -B drift-repro 5f4a3f088cd7018aef904a9f31ab6b071251733c && git merge --no-ff d972d18be0dd135ba8362c53bbeb9d4612cf5f81

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5f4a3f088cd7018aef904a9f31ab6b071251733c
```

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d972d18be0dd135ba8362c53bbeb9d4612cf5f81`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/automation/builtin-node-config.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.flow-builtin-node-config-values-refused.ts + packages/spec/src/automation/flow-node-config-refusals.ts (the shared judge: `flowNodeConfigRefusals`, `builtinValueJudged`), packages/spec/src/automation/flow.zod.ts (the `FlowSchema` superRefine door), packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/crud-nodes.ts (the `get_record` executor the rule is derived from), packages/spec/src/automation/flow-builtin-node-config-values.test.ts, .changeset/25302-get-record-limit-positive-integer.md, content/docs/references/automation/builtin-node-config.mdx. Remainder of the diff outside `hits`: none beyond those files (the lane seat's ACCEPT at TIER_DEFAULT covers the test, changeset and generated mdx as a standalone PR).

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Accept set narrowed — right.** `GetRecordConfigSchema.limit` goes `z.number().optional()` → `z.number().int().positive().optional()`. Under zod `^4.6.5` (spec's dependency) `.int()` is the safe-integer check, so `2.5`, `0`, `-1`, `0.5` and `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER + 2` are all refused; every positive whole number and an absent `limit` parse unchanged. The premise holds in the cited executor: `crud-nodes.ts` parses against this very contract (`parseNodeConfig('get_record', …, GetRecordConfigSchema, …)`), then `if (limit && limit > 1)` hands `limit` to `data.find` as written, else `findOne`; nothing routes through `findData`, so no page-window normalizer judged it. The card's gap is real and this is the right door.
2. **Refusal reaches every door with one code and path — right.** `flowNodeConfigRefusals`' builtin value arm keeps a present-value issue unless a carve-out applies; none does for `limit` (not a region slot, not a ledger `value`/`predicate` slot, not in `RUN_RESOLVED_KEYS`, not a value/text slot with its own judge). The `seen` set collapses `0.5`'s two zod issues (`not_integer` + `too_small`) into one `node-config-refused-by-contract` at `limit`; `FlowSchema`'s superRefine anchors it as a `custom` issue at `nodes.N.config.limit`. `defineStack` (422 `STACK_SCHEMA_INVALID`), the registered `flow` metadata-type schema, `registerFlow`, `objectstack validate`/`compile` and artifact parse all call this one judge, as the PR body says. No consumer code change is needed and none is made.
3. **Public surface — right.** Committed generated reference `content/docs/references/automation/builtin-node-config.mdx` is regenerated (`number` → `integer`, positive). The JSON Schema under `packages/spec/json-schema/` is gitignored and rebuilt by `gen:schema` (`.gitignore` lines 62–63), so its `type: integer` / `exclusiveMinimum: 0` is a build output, not a committed file; no other committed doc describes `get_record.limit` as a plain number. CHANGELOG mentions are historical.
4. **QueryPageWindowSchema deliberately not reused — right.** It is `int().nonnegative()`; `0` means "total only" at a list door, while `get_record` always reads at least one row. A separate bound with TSDoc stating why is the correct call; reusing it would have admitted `0` and silently preserved the `findOne` fallthrough.
5. **ADR-0087 disposition — right.** `not-required (already-registered flow-builtin-node-config-values-refused)` names a genuinely pre-existing D3 entry (not one this diff adds), and the entry is amended rather than left stale: `surface` (the added text carries no backtick and no pipe, as the file's header rule requires for `build-upgrade-guide.ts`), `replacement` and `reason` now name the `get_record` `limit` range, and the header comment records the one semantic difference (such a node used to run rather than fail). No D2 conversion is correct: the intended count is unknowable. The entry has no `relevantWhen`, so `objectstack migrate meta` lists it by construction, which is what the changeset's "reports it under `flow-builtin-node-config-values-refused`" amounts to. `registry.ts.template`'s narrative paragraph for this id is example-based and not made wrong; leaving it is acceptable.
6. **Executor behaviour after the change — right.** `if (limit && limit > 1)` is now exact (absent, or a whole number of at least 1). The executor's form descriptor `limit: { type: 'integer', title: 'Limit' }` has no `minimum`, so a designer form can still offer `0`; that reaches the save door and is refused loudly at `nodes.N.config.limit`. Outside the claimed file surface; see ③.
7. **Tests — right.** New probes at the judge (2.5 / 0 / -1 at `limit`), a `[#25302]` block covering `FlowSchema` in the contract's words, `defineStack` code+status+path for five values, the save-door schema, and lit controls (1, 2, 200, no `limit`). The reported ablation (10 failed / 59 passed with `int().positive()` removed) matches exactly the 10 refusal cases.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/25302-get-record-limit-positive-integer.md`: `@objectstack/spec: minor`, `fix(spec)!:` title, **BREAKING** declared with FROM → TO → Fix → Unchanged, data-at-rest behaviour and producer measurement. `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` on both the changeset and the PR body, matching triage's ruling (p1, protocol narrowing handled in 18.x with no retirement stage, `minor`). The diff publishes exactly a narrowing of a published schema and nothing else (no widening, no new export). Level and clause lines are correct. `Check Changeset`: success.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions: []` — none to answer.
- Dev out-of-scope finding (form descriptor `limit` without `minimum` in `crud-nodes.ts`, "noted, not filed"): **escalated, non-blocking.** Declared ≠ enforced does not bite (the save door refuses loudly, naming the key), but the Studio form now offers a value the save always refuses. That is a lower-grade authoring trap and belongs on a card (`area:workflow`, suggested p3: add `minimum: 1` to the form descriptor). Not a defect of this PR's surface.
- `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` NOT MEASURED locally, left to CI: answered by `Lint & Repo Gates` = success on this head.
- `Branch:` is `claude/project-thread-kdrs5c` rather than `claude/issue-25302-slug`; the claim comment explains the platform constraint, and the branch-claim gate (`The card this PR closes must claim this branch`) is success.
- Check-runs on `d972d18b` at review time (2026-10-23T03:05Z): 39 of 41 completed; every completed run is success or `skipped` (opt-in / matrix shells). **`Test Core (2/6)` and `Test Core (3/6)` are still in_progress.** The verdict below judges the completed gates plus the read diff; the two shards must finish green before merge, and a red one re-opens this record.
